_note: Deterministic gap probes (gaps.py). Each probe fires only if its rule finds no coverage; statements are limited to the examined sources. Classification comes from the rule result, not from this file.

probes.topic: Smoke detection with pre-fire (pyrolysis) smoke at elevated oxygen (>= 30% O2)
probes.rule_text: no detector-evaluating pyrolysis-smoke investigation profile with O2 max >= 30%; any unknown O2 -> INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION

statement.EVIDENCE_GAP: Within the examined sources, no spacecraft smoke-detector test with pre-fire (pyrolysis) smoke was run at elevated oxygen: SAME, SAME-R and the 2020 ground study used ordinary air at 21% O2, while the planned lunar habitat atmosphere is 34% O2 at 8.2 psi.
statement.INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION: Within the examined sources, the test atmosphere of at least one detector-evaluating pyrolysis investigation is not documented, so an elevated-oxygen gap cannot be asserted or excluded.

probes.detail: The SAME/SAME-R atmosphere is inferred from the glovebox facility description (21% O2, 14.7 psi) because the experiment reports state only 'air'. Saffire IV-VI did measure flaming-fire smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor at up to 0.31 O2 mole fraction and 541 mbar, so flaming smoke at exploration-like atmospheres is partly covered; pyrolysis smoke and the ISS or Shuttle detectors are not.

probes.topic: Smoke detection with pyrolysis smoke at reduced cabin pressure (<= 10.2 psi / 70.3 kPa)
probes.rule_text: no detector-evaluating pyrolysis-smoke investigation profile with pressure min <= 70.3 kPa; any unknown pressure -> INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION

statement.EVIDENCE_GAP: Within the examined sources, no smoke-detector test with pyrolysis smoke was run at reduced pressure: the detector-evaluating pyrolysis tests ran at 14.7 psi, while Gateway HALO is nominally 10.2 psi and the planned lunar habitat 8.2 psi.
statement.INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION: Within the examined sources, the test pressure of at least one detector-evaluating pyrolysis investigation is not documented, so a reduced-pressure gap cannot be asserted or excluded.

probes.detail: An ionization detector's baseline changes at low pressure and must be characterised, and most reference aerosol instruments have limited use below Earth-ambient pressure. Saffire IV-VI flaming tests reached 541 mbar with a commercial ionization sensor.

probes.topic: Smoke production, transport and detection in lunar (partial) gravity
probes.rule_text: no detector-evaluating investigation profile at lunar/partial gravity

statement.EVIDENCE_GAP: Within the examined sources, no smoke-detector test or smoke-particle measurement was made in lunar or other partial gravity; the 2021 white paper lists the airflow dependence of particle size in lunar gravity as unknown, and a 2023 NASA study addressed detector placement only by simulation.
statement.INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION: Within the examined sources, the gravity level of at least one detector-evaluating investigation is not documented.

probes.detail: Ground facilities give only seconds of lunar gravity (drop-tower centrifuge 5.2 s, parabolic flights about 30 s). Treating partial-gravity behaviour as bounded by microgravity and 1 g results is a hypothesis, not evidence, for smoke transport and detection.
expected_future_sources: FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon)

probes.topic: Controlled false-alarm testing of spacecraft smoke detectors with cabin and lunar dust
probes.rule_text: no false_alarm record that comes from a controlled, directly observed test
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, no controlled test measures how often the ISS or Shuttle smoke detector false-alarms on cabin dust or lunar dust; false alarms are documented only as operational reports, and dust-discriminating detectors exist only as early prototypes.
probes.detail: False alarms (alarm without fire) are a different event from missed alarms. ISS background-aerosol data go back to DAFT; the 2025 dust-tolerant detector paper reports early polarimetric prototype results with a lunar simulant.

probes.topic: Heritage spacecraft smoke detectors exposed to flaming-fire smoke in microgravity
probes.rule_text: no microgravity detector test with flaming-fire smoke for the ISS or Shuttle smoke detector
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors were evaluated in microgravity only with pre-fire (pyrolysis) smoke, never with smoke from flaming fires; Saffire IV-VI measured flaming-fire smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor instead.
probes.detail: SAME and SAME-R heated samples below ignition to emulate an overheat event. Saffire IV-VI fires were large flaming burns in an uncrewed Cygnus.

probes.topic: ISS smoke-detector response to PMMA smoke
probes.rule_text: material/detector pair not tested in microgravity with an alarm evaluation
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the ISS smoke detector was never tested with PMMA smoke in microgravity and no alarm decision was evaluated for PMMA smoke; its only exposure was a single 1 g ground test that measured signal against smoke mass.
probes.detail: Saffire IV-VI burned PMMA in microgravity but measured smoke with a commercial ionization sensor and an aerosol monitor, not with the ISS detector. Model A (BASS-II PMMA flame spread) says nothing about smoke-detector response.

probes.topic: Smoke-detector response to lithium-ion battery smoke
probes.rule_text: material not tested with any smoke detector in microgravity with an alarm evaluation
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, no spacecraft smoke-detector test with lithium-ion battery smoke was found, although laptop battery fires are named among the most likely long-mission fire scenarios.
probes.detail: The 2021 white paper knew of only one study characterising laptop-scale battery smoke particles.

probes.topic: Kapton and Teflon detector response differs between SAME (2007) and SAME-R (2010)
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the ISS detector's response to Kapton and Teflon smoke differs strongly between the 2007 SAME and 2010 SAME-R campaigns, and no source explains why.
probes.detail: Kapton reached 2.0 V in every SAME run but in a minority of SAME-R runs, while Teflon went the other way; the measured counts are in the cited records.

probes.topic: Shuttle detector: 'strong signal in all tests' vs 'some runs below alarm boundary'
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the 2010 SAME report and the 2018 paper disagree on whether the Space Shuttle ionization detector responded to all SAME smokes; the difference may come from test sets and criteria and is unresolved.

probes.topic: Size increase of zero-flow smoke reported with different magnitudes
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the zero-flow particle-size increase is reported as 30 % to 40 %, as 2 to 3 times and as 1.7 times on average; the direction agrees but the magnitude is unresolved.

probes.topic: Unaged Teflon row of the 2012 SAME-2 particle-size table is internally inconsistent
probes.statement: Within the examined sources, the unaged Teflon row of the 2012 particle-size table cannot be reproduced from its own geometric values; separate averaging of each statistic is a likely but undocumented cause.
